title: fix: read a scoped mutation base past a large deleted file
headline: The planted-bug check reads a branch that deletes a large file as the commits they are, so a PR that removes many megabytes still has its new tests measured. Nothing a project installs changes.
alignment: v1.43.3 is the third pull request of build 18: PR 55 deletes 10 MB of backups, and main's copy of this check, which judges it, measured none of its new tests.

items.text: A scoped mutation run leaves deleted files out of the diff it reads and gives git's output room, so a large deletion no longer reads as a base that is no commit.
items.where: CI's test check on a PR that deletes a large file

verification: The new test deletes a 2 MB file and changes one line; the scoped count finds the one flip.
The other scoped-run test still refuses a base that is no commit or reads as a git option.

decisions.decision: Its own pull request, ahead of PR 55
decisions.why: CI judges a PR with main's copy of this check, so the fix must be on main before PR 55's tests can be measured.

decisions.decision: Leave deletions out rather than only raise the buffer
decisions.why: A deleted file adds no line to flip, so reading it costs memory for nothing; the larger buffer covers a large addition.

upgrading: Nothing to do: install copies none of these files.

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Not touched: the base is still read as a commit, never as an option

tests.flips: declared tests at 2d5c73a and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
